newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik group seized four Russian journalists.
newsitem.headline: Tajik group seized four Russian journalists.

text.p: A group of Tajik rebels which seized four U.N. observers earlier this week has detained four Russian reporters who went to investigate the kidnapping, a spokesman with the U.N. mission in Dushanbe said on Wednesday.

"We have radio contact with our people and we have information that four journalists have been detained," the spokesman said. The group of reporters, two men and two women, were heading for the rebel district when they were seized.

The reporters had been planning to rendevous with an armed group led by Rizvon Sadirov, who once fought for the former Soviet republic's Islamic opposition against the secular government but whose loyalties now are unclear.
Sadirov's group seized the U.N. military observers on Tuesday, demanding safe passage for its members based in neighbouring Afghanistan.
The U.N. has demanded the immediate release of the hostages, an Austrian, a Ukrainian, two Swiss nationals and an interpreter and it says that the Austrian is seriously ill.

The United Nations Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT) has about 45 military personnel in the republic to observe a fragile peace agreement aimed at ending a bitter four-year civil war. Moscow peace talks are due on February 26.
